fatal_errors: The proposed coated refractory high-entropy alloy does not reconstruct the target bulk CoCrFeNiMox-Ni/MoS2-Ag-Cr2O3 composite or the intervention of varying Mo content.

The cited evidence concerns nanoprecipitation strengthening in tungsten refractory high-entropy alloys and provides no support for h-BN deposition, coating adhesion, self-lubrication, or wide-temperature tribological performance.
The hypothesis omits the target's temperature-dependent lubrication transition from MoS2/Ag films to NiO and silver-molybdate glaze formation.
explanation: The response recognizes the broad need to combine high-temperature strength with low friction and proposes a testable coated-versus-uncoated experiment. However, it substitutes an unsupported surface-coating concept for the target spark-plasma-sintered multiphase composite. It does not identify the CoCrFeNiMox matrix, Ni-coated MoS2, Ag, Cr2O3, Mo-induced lattice distortion and sigma phase, or the specified room-temperature-to-800 °C dry-sliding conditions. Its generic interfacial-film mechanism only weakly overlaps with the target tribofilm concept. Most importantly, E1 supports refractory-alloy strength but not the hypothesized coating or tribological claims, so the proposed material is not evidence-grounded.
